candidates.angle: aviyam, everlasting, means the disgrace never ends
Krishna shifts from inner duty to public opinion
candidates.evidence: कथयिष्यन्ति तेऽव्ययाम् (will speak of your everlasting)

candidates.angle: Krishna contrasts death with disgrace for an honored man

en.intro: Krishna continues his argument by warning Arjuna about the world outside the chariot. Listen for the exact comparison he makes between dying and living with shame.
en.notice: Krishna says the disgrace will be aviyam, everlasting. For a man honored as you are, that endless shame is worse than death. He shifts the argument from your inner duty to how the world will judge you.
en.next: The great warriors will think you withdrew from battle out of fear, and those who once held you in high regard will see you as small.
en.next_alt: The great warriors will think you withdrew from battle out of fear, and those who once held you in high regard will see you as small.

en.meaning: And all beings will speak of your everlasting disgrace. For an honored person, disgrace is worse than death.

hi.intro: कृष्ण अब अर्जुन की चिंता को बाहर की दुनिया की ओर मोड़ते हैं। सुनिए, वे मृत्यु और अपमान की तुलना कैसे करते हैं।
hi.meaning: और सब प्राणी भी तेरी सदा रहनेवाली अपकीर्तिका कथन करेंगे। वह अपकीर्ति सम्मानित मनुष्यके लिये मृत्युसे भी बढ़कर दुःखदायी होती है

issues: meaning_changed: "और सब प्राणी भी तेरी सदा रहनेवाली अपकीर्तिका कथन अर्थात निंदा करेंगे ।" (The Hindi translation adds the word 'नিন্দা' (censure/blame/slander). The source word is 'कथयिष्यन्ति' (will speak/narrate), which means people will speak of the disgrace, not necessarily censure it. This addition softens and changes the meaning from 'speaking of' to 'blaming/censuring'.)
